ground_truth.title: Looking for a place to work? Here are 9 co-working spots around Milwaukee
ground_truth.author: Sarah Hauer
ground_truth.main_content:
Entrepreneurs and remote workers are driving the need for co-working spaces where you can rent a desk, or a few, for a growing business.

In the Milwaukee area, a handful of new co-working spaces have opened in the past year dedicated to entrepreneurs, women business owners and water technology. The number of co-working spaces worldwide has more than doubled in the past three years, according to an Emergent Research report. The small business research firm predicts the number of co-working spaces worldwide will double again by 2022.

Whether you're turning a side hustle into a full-time gig or you're a digital nomad who needs to get out of the house, here are nine co-working spaces around Milwaukee. All have vacancies.

5Wise

A self-governing co-working space on National Ave., 5Wise, is a low-cost and flexible option. A membership to 5Wise is $50 a month. Additional memberships can be added on for $25 a month. It offers month-to-month memberships and opened last summer.

Members have 24/7 access to the co-working space and can reserve the meeting areas. High-speed internet, basic office supplies and printing are included. 5Wise also has Chromebooks and other technology for members' use. Coffee, tea and Hamm's beer are also stocked.

Website: 5wise.co

Address: 3524 W. National Ave.

Hudson Business Lounge

In the heart of Milwaukee's Historic Third Ward, the Hudson Business Lounge has some of the most expansive options. Yes, it has desks and offices for rent. There are long tables, standing tables, cubicles and phone booths. Meeting rooms — from a solo office to a 15-person conference room — also are bookable by the hour. The Hudson sets itself apart with event space, a cafe and catering options.

The Hudson has a lot of different options for using its space, from a basic day pass ($29) to an unlimited monthly membership ($269 to $459). Members have access to the work center during operating hours, coffee, Wi-Fi, printing and social events.

Website: thehudson.org

Address: 310 E. Buffalo St.

Ironwood

The Ironwood has 15 spaces that range in size from a one-person office to a multi-desk space. All the offices are private but enclosed with glass. The smallest is 150 square feet while the largest is 3,500.

Rent includes printing, access to conference rooms, Wi-Fi and an open kitchen with pastries brought in daily. Tenants can sign short-term leases and enter as they please. The building has parking spots. In some rooms, a desk rental goes for $200 a month, while a private office is $600 a month. A four-person office costs $1,600.

Website: ironwoodoffice.com

Address: 5205 N. Ironwood Road, Glendale

MalamaDoe

MalamaDoe isn't trying to be fancy — it wants to be accessible for women and encourage their business dreams. MalamaDoe in Shorewood is a community for female entrepreneurs with a co-working space. The idea is to support women entrepreneurs and help launch their businesses. Membership costs between $150 and $180 a month. I t comes with a key for 24/7 access. MalamaDoe, which opened in the spring of last year, is just for women.

Members can use the Wi-Fi, conference rooms, a greenscreen wall and whiteboards. In meeting its goal of supporting female entrepreneurship, MalamaDoe hosts guests speakers and its members are automatically a part of the Shorewood Business Improvement District.

Website: malamadoe.com

Address: 4465 N. Oakland Ave., Suite 201, Shorewood

Oasis Coworking Community

The Oasis Coworking Community housed within the Global Water Center is built for businesses focused on water technology. The center has eight reserved desks and four shared desks with plans to expand the co-working community. A shared desk is $250 a month, while a reserved desk is $325 a month.

Renting space in Oasis comes with high-speed internet, printing, storage and mail services. Since it's housed within the Global Water Center, renters also can use the auditorium and meeting rooms. Tenants can access the space 24/7.

Website: thewatercouncil.com/oasis

Address: Global Water Center, 247 W. Freshwater Way

The Hive

A downtown co-working space that opened last fall, The Hive, is looking to help shape the startup scene in Milwaukee. The Hive has four private offices and five shared desks in addition to common areas and meeting rooms. Membership includes printing, coffee, Wi-Fi, snacks and beer.

The Hive offers month-to-month plans starting at $200 a month for 24/7 access. A dedicated desk plan starts at $275 a month and a private office is $550 a month. Day passes to work in The Hive are $15. Right now, it's offering a 10-pack of single day passes for $125.

Website: thehivemke.com

Address: 720 N. Milwaukee St.

Ward4

Ward4 was founded to be a destination for innovation and technology in Milwaukee. It houses the startup accelerator gener8tor. Members have 24/7 access to Ward4, event space and meeting rooms. Ward4 also has projectors, whiteboards and printing services. Members get a mailing address, too.

Membership is $250 a month with a yearlong contract or $300 for a month-to-month deal. Members can get a single desk, a private office or an entire suite. Day passes for single desks are $30.

Website: ward4mke.com

Address: 313 N. Plankinton Ave., Suite 205

Water Street office and co-working

This downtown space has some of the larger offices in Milwaukee's co-working scene. Right on Water St., it has a combination of private offices and co-working desks. The offices range in size from a single desk to six-user mini-suites.

Rent starts at $449 a month and goes up to $1,999 a month. The rental fees include internet, phone, a receptionist, conference room use and even a "never-ending fruit table." The building also has parking spots available for $50 a month.

Website: s implefastflexible.com

Address: 1123 N. Water St.

Workspace

Workspace in Brookfield has month-to-month options for entrepreneurs looking for a place to work and access to experts. Members get 24-7 access to Workspace, its conference rooms, Wi-Fi, printing and other services.

Pick a desk for a day with an open-desk membership for $150 a month. A dedicated desk in the open co-working area is $275 a month. A private office starts at $650 a month. The community holds casual events for members and schedules meeting with potential investors and experts.

Website: workspaces.us

Address: 250 N. Sunnyslope Road, Suite 200, Brookfield
